item.title: Germany Implements NIS2- Registration Portal Will Open on January 6, 2026
item.description: With the official enactment of the NIS-2 Implementation Act, Germany has taken a major step toward modernizing its cybersecurity framework. Starting from 6 December 2025, stricter requirements will apply to both federal administration and thousands of private companies. item.title: Countdown to 2026- Essential Paid Leave, Earned Sick and Safe Time Updates for Minnesota Employers
item.description: Takeaways Starting 01.01.26, Minnesota’s Paid Leave law provides employees up to 20 weeks of leave for qualifying reasons. The law includes immediate requirements for posting and individual notice. Minneapolis and Saint Paul recently amended their Earned Sick and Safe Time ordinances to align more closely with Minnesota’s statewide law. item.title: SEC Extends Compliance Date for Short Position Reporting Rule
item.description: Highlights: Institutional investment managers now have until Jan. 2, 2028 to begin monthly reporting under Rule 13f-2/Form SHO, and securities lenders also receive an extension for Rule 10c-1a disclosures as specified in the order. item.title: State Department Adds H-1B/H-4 Visa Applicants to Expanded Online Presence Screening List
item.description: The State Department announced that as of December 15, 2025, applicants for H-1B and H-4 (dependent) visas at US consular posts will undergo advanced screening of their online presence. This expanded screening is already in place for those applying for F, M, and J nonimmigrant visas as of June 2025. This new process will apply even if the applicant is renewing a previously-issued visa. item.title: Fine Line - Fourth Circuit Joins Other Courts In Narrowly Interpreting Who Qualifies As An NLRA-Exempt Manager
item.description: On December 1, 2025, in NLRB v. Constellis, LLC, a unanimous Fourth Circuit panel joined other federal appellate courts in narrowly interpreting the National Labor Relations Act’s (“NLRA” or the “Act”) judge-made managerial exception, which carves out certain high-level employees from the NLRA’s protections.
